newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe echoes Chirac call on more French tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Juppe echoes Chirac call on more French tax cuts.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday the idea of further tax cuts could be looked into if the economy picked up as planned, according to Gilles de Robien, head of the UDF group in the National Assembly.
De Robien also cited Juppe as raising the possibility of implementing an existing 75-billion-franc package of income tax cuts in four years rather than five.
The prime minister underlined that "we would have to look at another cut in taxes" if the economic upturn came through, de Robien said after Juppe spoke to UDF deputies.
President Jacques Chirac spoke of going further in cutting taxes during a television interview last Thursday and said he favoured doing it as soon as possible.
De Robien also reported Juppe as raising the possibility of a cut in value added tax, which was hiked by the government in July 1995 to 20.6 percent from 18.6 percent.
